note: Declared-correct output for the synthetic corpus. Written from what each document SAYS, not from what the pipeline currently produces -- an expectation copied from actual output can only ever pass, and would test nothing. Entries that the pipeline is known to fail are kept, and their failure is reported.

how_to_read.jurisdiction: exact match required against the chunks' jurisdiction metadata
how_to_read.language: the result's language must be one of these values; 'mixed' is listed alongside a specific script where either answer is defensible for a parallel bilingual document
how_to_read.required_clause_ids: every id listed must appear among the emitted chunks' structure.clause_id. Extra ids are allowed -- a document may legitimately carry structure beyond what is enumerated here
how_to_read.tables_expected: count of distinct tables the document contains, counted by hand from the source
how_to_read.min_chunks: a floor, not a target: below this the document was clearly under-segmented

synthetic_contract_ar.docx.why: A nine-article Arabic supply contract in DOCX. DOCX stores logical text, so this is the control against which the PDF renderings of the same material are read.

synthetic_contract_bilingual.pdf.why: The same contract as a PDF. Its Arabic headings read 'المادة (1): التعريفات' on the page, so art_1..art_7 is the correct answer. KNOWN TO FAIL: the generator paints Arabic as visually-ordered presentation forms, the article number lands at the wrong end of the heading, and the ids degrade to sec_* built from mangled text. Kept as a failing expectation on purpose -- it is the measurement of that limitation.

synthetic_lease_bilingual.docx.why: A lease is a contract; the type must not degrade to 'unknown' merely because the word 'lease' is used instead of 'agreement'.

synthetic_memo_mixed.txt.why: An internal memo, not a contract. Distinguishing the two matters to M5, which should not be asked to extract obligations from correspondence.

synthetic_statute_ar.txt.why: Includes 'المادة 7 مكرر' -- the bis-article convention. A numbering scheme that only understands integers silently merges it into article 7.

synthetic_visual_order_ar.txt.why: Same statute, stored in visual order. The correct answer is identical to synthetic_statute_ar.txt -- that is the point of the pair. PARTIAL FAILURE EXPECTED: articles whose heading line is reversed are not recovered.

stress_nested_clauses_ar.pdf.why: Five levels of numbering. The nesting must be preserved as a hierarchy, not flattened: M5 needs to know that 5.2.1.b.ii sits under 5.2, because the obligation it carries is qualified by 5.2's scope.

stress_inline_bilingual.pdf.why: Five numbered memo paragraphs. KNOWN TO FAIL: every paragraph opens with an Arabic run, so the visual-order storage puts each number at the end of its line and no marker is found. Kept as a failing expectation -- this is the sharpest measurement of the visual-order limitation in the corpus.

stress_exhibits_footnotes.pdf.why: Four parallel numbering systems: Articles, lettered Exhibits, roman Appendices and numbered Schedules. All four must survive; an annex is not a clause of the article that precedes it.

stress_table_pagebreak.pdf.why: One logical 30-row table split by a page break. document_type is left unconstrained: a bare instalment schedule with no operative language is genuinely ambiguous, and forcing a guess would be worse than 'unknown'.

synthetic_table_page.png.why: Borderless bilingual table as an image. Neither Docling nor PyMuPDF sees an OCR'd page, so this is the fixture that measures table reconstruction from OCR geometry.

stress_table_ruled_ar.png.why: Fully ruled 5x3 table -- the easy case, and the control for the two harder ones.

stress_table_wide_en.png.why: Six borderless columns with narrow gutters: tests cell splitting when the column gap approaches the word gap.

stress_table_sparse_bilingual.png.why: Empty cells in every column: a reconstructor that assumes full rows shifts contents left instead of emitting a gap.
